extracted.intended_audience: comic creators, small-press publishers, cartoonists submitting work to the Ignatz Awards / Small Press Expo
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and eligibility criteria for submitting comics, graphic novels, minicomics, anthologies, collections, and related categories (Artist, Series, Story, Promising New Talent) to the Ignatz Awards at Small Press Expo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary category selection / mutual exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.description: You may submit an entry for any one of these six mutually exclusive categories for which a work may be eligible: Anthology, Comic, Minicomic, Graphic Novel, Collection, Online Comic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These six are mutually exclusive; choose the single primary category appropriate to the work. In addition to one of the above categories, you can also submit your work to any or all of the additional categories (Artist, Series, Stories, Promising New Talent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Anthology definition
rubrics_metrics.description: This award recognizes a book or other collection of selected writings by various writers usually in the same literary form, of the same period, or on the same subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a book of comics by various cartoonists selected from several books by many cartoonists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection definition
rubrics_metrics.description: This award recognizes a book of selected short comics from various prior publications by the same cartoonist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The comics may constitute a single story, but as the parts were previously published, the story line would not be considered for the Graphic Novel category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comic (single-issue) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A comic nominated in this category should represent the best marriage of both art and story in a single issue of a comic that are professionally published in the traditional floppy comic format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to reflect the traditional floppy comic format familiar to superhero comics; emphasizes balance of art and story in a single issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic Novel definition (length & publication status)
rubrics_metrics.description: A nomination for this category is for previously unpublished material of substantial length intended to be read as a single work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic novels are distinguished from individual comics by being generally over 48 pages and are usually case or perfect bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minicomic definition (self-published/non-professional)
rubrics_metrics.description: This category includes both one-shots and series. Minicomics are defined as comics that are not 'professionally' published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minicomics are usually printed at the local copy store or via a risograph, hand stapled, and predominantly self-distributed and are not solicited through major distributors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online Comic eligibility and format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This category is for web based comics. A nominee can be an individual comic, continuing storyline comic or strips.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a work to be eligible it must be published on the web prior to appearing in print format. Nominated sites must also adhere to the same publishing timeline as the categories for print material. Works posted on web pages outside the timeline are not eligible. Nominated sites can utilize animation but should still be recognizable as a comic — 'If you read it, it’s a comic. If you watch it, it’s animation.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist category criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations for this category reflect the best execution of graphic skill by an individual within the comic medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus is on graphic/artistic execution rather than solely on writing or format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Series category criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: A nomination in this category should be for a series that the Juror feels exhibits a consistent level of quality as a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good individual story does not necessarily translate into a nomination for the entire series; jurors evaluate the series-level consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story category criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: This category is for outstanding storytelling in a comic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may be an individual issue within a series, a one-shot, or a single story within an anthology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promising New Talent eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A person nominated should be someone new to the industry whose work deserves more recognition than it currently receives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past nominees for the Ignatz Award cannot be nominated in this category. Nominations should include the title of the individual’s latest work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: Works eligible for the 2026 Ignatz Awards have to be published between June 1, 2026 and May 31, 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication date is generally determined by date of distribution. (Note: ensure your work's distribution date falls within the stated window.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Online submission window
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted online between April 1 and May 31st 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Late submissions outside this window will be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: File format and size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PDF file formats only. No file above 200meg.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can submit more than one file per work but PLEASE do not submit print-ready files.

rubrics_metrics.name: File naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: File naming conventions differ by category and must be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Mini-comics, Comics, Series, Story, Artist, Promising New Talent and Graphic Novels: CreatorLastName.CreatorFirstName.Comic_Title.IssueNumber.Publisher.PubMonthPubYear.pdf (omit IssueNumber if none; if self published, put Self as the Publisher). For anthologies and collections: EditorLastName.EditorFirstName.Comic_Title..Publisher.PubMonthPubYear.pdf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing copy for SPX Collection at the Library of Congress
rubrics_metrics.description: Each submittor must mail a copy to be included in the SPX Collection at the Library of Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves works for future generations and provides a copy at the show if your work is nominated. If a work is submitted for more than one category, please send only one copy. Mailing address and contact information are provided on the submission page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and questions procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions about submissions should be emailed to ignatzawards@smallpressexpo.com.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow a few days for a response.
